Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  - Left-sided reduced hearing for ~6 weeks, intermittent.
  - Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in the left ear; patient stated some things “trigger it,” then stated watching TV/listening to music “solves” the ringing (conflict noted).
  - Intermittent mild dizziness/off-balance; not true room-spinning vertigo; no associated nausea reported.
  - No ear pain reported. No ear discharge reported. No fever reported. Ear itchiness not recorded.
  - Prior brief hearing issue about 1 year ago lasting a couple of days.
  - Denies using cotton buds to clean ears.

Management Plan

- Arrange in-person appointment within 4–5 days for ear examination (otoscopy) to assess for cerumen impaction or other causes of unilateral hearing loss and tinnitus.
- Tinnitus education: Link to information provided in visit notes; patient asked to review before the in-person appointment.
- Safety netting: Not considered an emergency. Advised to book another appointment if symptoms worsen or any new concerns arise before the scheduled visit.
- Logistics: Patient to call the support team to book the face-to-face appointment.
- Education: Advised not to use cotton buds for ear cleaning.

Quality checks

- Missing clinically expected elements: Past medical history; medication list and allergies; vitals (BP, pulse); height/weight/BMI; immunization review; alcohol/smoking/substance history; mental health screening; sexual and reproductive health history; vision screen; urinalysis; cardiovascular/neurological review; documented hearing test/audiometry.
- Internal contradictions: Patient described TV/music as “triggers” for tinnitus, then stated TV/music “solves” the ringing.
- Transcript quality: Some responses were brief or unclear; portions of the audio appear incomplete (e.g., answers about itchiness and palpitations not clearly recorded).
